# Rome 46 BC – Economy & finance

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from eras/europe-46bc-rome.yaml — do not edit -->

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Coinage (stamped metal money)** [`coinage`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coinage.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Silver denarius of four sesterces, struck at 84 to the pound; Caesar strikes gold aurei in quantity from his Gallic and treasury gold. Bronze small change is old and worn. Local: mint at the temple of Juno Moneta on the Arx.
- **Double-entry bookkeeping** [`double_entry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/double_entry.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Every head of household keeps a daybook and a ledger of receipts and payments; bankers' books are evidence in court. Single entry, Roman numerals, no capital account.
- **Interest-bearing loans, pledges and limits on debt bondage** [`interest_loans_collateral`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/interest_loans_collateral.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The legal ceiling is 1% a month. Provincials paid far more: Brutus' agents charged Salamis in Cyprus 48%. Debt bondage is abolished; a bankrupt loses property and honour.
- **Deposit banking and bills of exchange** [`banking_credit`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/banking_credit.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Argentarii at the Forum take deposits, pay on written order and finance auctions. Senators lend through agents. Funds move between cities by book transfer (permutatio). No notes or traded bills. Local: bankers' stalls (tabernae argentariae) on the Forum; T. Pomponius Atticus. Elsewhere: Ptolemaic Egypt, royal banks with transfers between accounts.
- **Paper money** [`paper_money`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/paper_money.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. No paper. Large sums already pass as book debts (nomina), but money means silver and gold.
- **Money supply, debasement and inflation** [`quantity_theory_inflation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/quantity_theory_inflation.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. In 49–47 BC coin vanished into hoards and land prices collapsed. Caesar had property valued at pre-war prices and limited cash holdings to 60,000 sesterces. Nobody theorises it.
- **Risk-sharing partnership (commenda, mudaraba)** [`partnership_commenda`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/partnership_commenda.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. In a societas partners share profit and loss as agreed; it ends when a partner dies. Ventures also run on sea loans and slaves trading with the master's capital (peculium).
- **Joint-stock company and limited liability** [`joint_stock_company`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/joint_stock_company.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept low. Companies of publicani farm taxes and public contracts, with shares (partes) held by outside investors, senators included through fronts. They outlast a partner's death. Ordinary trade has nothing like it. Local: the equites who run the tax companies; C. Rabirius Postumus, financier.
- **Insurance (marine, fire, life)** [`insurance`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/insurance.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. A sea loan is cancelled if the ship is lost, at high interest. In 215 BC the state took the sea risk for army contractors and was cheated. No premiums.
- **Life tables and the pricing of annuities** [`life_tables_annuities`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/life_tables_annuities.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. The census records citizens' ages, but nobody tabulates deaths, and chance has no arithmetic.
- **Public debt and government bonds** [`public_debt_bonds`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_debt_bonds.md) — K2, use none, make hard, accept low. The state borrowed from citizens in the Hannibalic war and repaid in instalments and land. Caesar funds himself by booty, confiscated estates and 'loans' demanded from towns.
- **Stock exchange (securities market)** [`stock_exchange`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/stock_exchange.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept low. Shares in the tax companies change hands informally around the Forum; Cicero mentions their high price in 59 BC. No listed market.
- **Central bank and lender of last resort** [`central_bank`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/central_bank.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. In the credit crisis the remedy was decree: debts settled in property at old valuations, interest already paid deducted. Nobody lent into the panic.
- **Division of labour and specialisation** [`division_of_labour`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/division_of_labour.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept medium. Large slave households and workshops specialise finely, and Xenophon's remark on city trades is known. Practised, not theorised.
- **Comparative advantage and free trade** [`comparative_advantage_free_trade`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/comparative_advantage_free_trade.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Customs are low and for revenue. Italy's harbour dues, abolished in 60 BC, are restored by Caesar on foreign goods. Grain supply is politics, not trade theory.
- **Prices, supply and demand** [`price_mechanism_supply_demand`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/price_mechanism_supply_demand.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Grain rises when ships fail; hoarders get the blame and the state hands out grain. Cicero's De officiis (44 BC) debates whether a seller must reveal that more ships come.
- **Public granaries and price stabilisation (ever-normal granary)** [`ever_normal_granary`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/ever_normal_granary.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Tax grain from Sicily, Sardinia and Africa feeds the dole and is stored in warehouses by the Tiber wharf. It is distributed, not used to steady prices. Local: warehouses of the Sulpicii Galbae (later Horrea Galbana) near the Emporium; Puteoli. Elsewhere: Han China, ever-normal granaries (from 54 BC).
- **Income tax and progressive rates** [`progressive_income_tax`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/progressive_income_tax.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Citizens in Italy have paid no direct tax since 167 BC; the old tributum was a levy on census property. Provinces pay tithes and fixed sums.
- **Savings banks, credit and consumer cooperatives** [`cooperatives_savings_banks`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cooperatives_savings_banks.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept low. Burial clubs collect monthly dues and pay for funerals. Most clubs are banned just now.
- **Wealth as productivity; sustained economic growth** [`economic_growth_productivity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/economic_growth_productivity.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Wealth is land, slaves and booty; Caesar's Gallic gold lowered the price of gold in Italy. Saving labour gains an owner little while captives are cheap.
- **National income accounts (GDP)** [`national_accounts_gdp`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/national_accounts_gdp.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Census property classes and provincial tax totals are the only aggregates anyone has.
- **Fighting slumps by sustaining demand (Keynesian policy)** [`aggregate_demand_countercyclical_policy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/aggregate_demand_countercyclical_policy.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Caesar's building works, games, rent remission and veterans' bounties put money among the plebs, as politics. The crisis is thought of as debt and scarce coin.
